pages.summary: A cell array of empty matrices.
body: A cell array holds values of any kinds and sizes, one in each cell: numbers, text, other cell arrays. Curly braces reach the contents (`C{2}`), round brackets select cells and give a smaller cell array (`C(2)`). `cell(m, n)` makes room for `m`-by-`n` cells, each holding `[]`, to be filled in later; cell arrays are also written directly, as `{1, 'two', [3 4]}`.
syntax: An n-by-n cell array of empty matrices.

examples.title: Braces and brackets
Texts of different lengths
examples.output:
Ann          3 letters
Bartholomew  11 letters
Cy           2 letters

pages.summary: A struct, from field names and values; a cell value makes a struct array.
body: A struct groups values under names, its fields: `s.name` reads or sets one. Fields can also be added one at a time by assignment, without `struct`. A cell array as a value makes a struct array with an element for each cell, so to store a cell array itself in a field, wrap it in another pair of braces.

examples.title: Fields by name, and by assignment
examples.output:
s = 

  struct with fields:

    name: 'Ada'
    year: 1815

ans =

        1815

examples.title: A cell array as one value

pages.summary: The names of a struct's fields, as a cell column.
body: In the order the fields were added. With dynamic field names, `s.(name)`, the fields can be visited one by one.

examples.title: The names, and visiting each field

pages.summary: True when a struct has a field (or which of several it has).
body: With one name, true or false; with a cell array of names, an answer for each. Often used to give a default for an option a caller left out.
syntax: For each name of a cell array.

examples.title: A default for a missing option
examples.output:
opts = 

  struct with fields:

        tol: 1.0000e-06
    maxIter: 100

pages.summary: Call a function on the contents of every cell.
body: Calls the function once for each cell and collects the results. When every result is a scalar they make an array of the cell array's size; otherwise ask for `'UniformOutput', false` and the results come back in a cell array. Several cell arrays of the same size give the function several inputs.
syntax: `fun(C{k})` for each cell, as an array.
The results in a cell array.
Two outputs of `fun` for each cell.

examples.title: The length of each text, and which are empty
Results that are not scalars

pages.summary: Call a function on every element of arrays.
body: Like `cellfun`, but over the elements of ordinary arrays (or struct arrays). Element-wise operators are faster where they apply; `arrayfun` helps when the function works only on one value at a time, such as one that builds text or calls a solver.
syntax: `fun(X(k))` for each element, as an array.
The results in a cell array.

examples.title: A function of one value at a time
Text for each element
examples.code: labels = arrayfun(@(t) sprintf('%.1f s', t), [0.5 1 2], 'UniformOutput', false)

examples.title: A root for each parameter
examples.intro: `fzero` solves for one value at a time.

c = [1 2 3];
x = arrayfun(@(ci) fzero(@(x) x.^3 + x - ci, 1), c)
